concepts.description: Modeling a linear relationship between inputs and a target by fitting coefficients to data. The lecture frames it as a least-squares problem.
concepts.name: Linear Regression

concepts.description: Choosing model parameters to minimize the sum of squared residuals between predictions and observed targets. It is the core optimization formulation behind linear regression in this lecture.
concepts.name: Least-Squares Problem

concepts.description: The linear system obtained by setting the gradient of the squared-error objective to zero, whose solution gives the least-squares coefficients.
concepts.name: Normal Equations

concepts.description: Splitting expected prediction error into bias, variance, and irreducible noise components, which explains how model complexity affects generalization.
concepts.name: Bias-Variance Decomposition

concepts.description: Adding an L2 penalty on coefficient magnitude to the least-squares objective, which stabilizes the solution and reduces overfitting.
concepts.name: Ridge Regularization

concepts.description: A factorization of the design matrix into an orthogonal and an upper-triangular matrix, used as a numerically stable way to solve least-squares problems.
concepts.name: QR Decomposition

concepts.description: Choosing among candidate models or regularization strengths based on their expected generalization error, guided by the bias-variance tradeoff.
concepts.name: Model Selection

concepts.description: Assessing the computational cost of solving the regression system, comparing how the normal equations and QR approaches scale with data size and feature count.
concepts.name: Big-O Analysis of Matrix Solves
